XcFirst.description: Supplies a name that a LATER enum would derive for itself. Each enum only knows its own names, so nothing here can see the clash coming.

XcSecond.description: Derives XcSecondX for value x. AddDecl dedupes by name and keeps the first declaration, so before this fix the constant was simply absent — not duplicated, not an error.

XcAaaImport.description: Supplies `time`, which nothing imports yet. XcZzzWhen's date-time property imports it LATER, so the clash only exists once generation ends; the constant is renamed then.

XcClaimsType.description: Supplies the name of a type generated after it. Type allocation used to see only other types, so XcTarget was declared under a name the constant already held and AddDecl dropped it.

XcHolder.description: Its own enum property asks for the name XcHolder while XcHolder is still being generated: registered as a type, not yet a declaration in the package.

XcZzzWhen.description: A date-time property maps to time.Time, importing `time` with no unmarshaler of its own to generate.
